newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Sao Paulo confirms will give up control of Banespa.
newsitem.headline: Sao Paulo confirms will give up control of Banespa.

text.p: Sao Paulo state governor Mario Covas acknowledged the state government will lose control of its bank Banespa under a refinancing package for the state's huge debt.
Covas refused to give details on how and when the refinancing plan will be unveiled but said the deal is in "its final phase."

The deal, expected to be announced this week, would involve the payment of 20 percent of Sao Paulo's debt through asset sales, while the remainder would be refinanced over 30 years, paying interest per year of six percent plus inflation.
The package would also include the transfer of Sao Paulo state's controlling stake in Banespa to the federal government, according to sources close to the deal.
Covas recognized the state government might be unable to recover the bank.
"I don't know whether the state will have conditions to regain control of the bank," he told reporters after a luncheon with bank executives at the Sao Paulo Stock Exchange (Bovespa).
Covas said Sao Paulo owes 20 billion reais to Banespa and has no means to pay off this debt.
He also said Banespa could have a private manager like Rio de Janeiro state bank Banerj, which has been managed by private bank Bozano, Simonsen and will be privatized later this year.
However, Covas refused to clarify if Banespa's fate would be its privatization.
He emphasized what is being negotiated is Sao Paulo's total debt, which includes debts with its banks Banespa, Nossa Caixa Nosso Banco and its outstanding debt in the form of public securities.
"Banespa is not under negotiations. The problem is not Banespa but Sao Paulo's debt," he said.
Sao Paulo's debt totals now 45 billion reais, of which 20 billion reais is owed to Banespa. The deal, however, will consider the state's debt at the end of March, which totalled 37 billion reais.
He said Sao Paulo deal will follow agreements already signed by Minas Gerais and Rio Grande do Sul states, which in September refinanced part of their debts.
Covas could not confirm or deny a press report saying Banespa showed a 786.3 million real net profit in the first nine months.
Banespa, Brazil's largest state bank, has been under Central Bank management since December 1994.
